children: Grains are having a quiet day with weekly export sales at the upper end of estimates and no flash sales. "There is little fundamental reason for the grains to sustain rallies," says Brian Hoops of Midwest Market Solutions. However, farmer selling is starting to slow, implying more stable or slightly firmer local cash prices, "which is usually friendly for futures," he adds."Seasonal tendencies are lower for wheat and corn as this is not normally a bullish time frame for the grain markets." Corn is off 0.7% on CBOT. Wheat is up 0.4%. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
